0035c5f8 xplat/caffe2/caffe2/operators/conv_transpose_op.cc
0035c62c The ConvTranspose op takes an input data tensor $X$, an input weight tensor $filter$, and optionally an input bias tensor $bias$. It then computes the transposed convolution, sometimes referred to as deconvolution, and produces a single output tensor $Y$. The hyperparameters of the op such as kernel size, stride, and padding are specified as args. At each stride, the filter is deconvolved with a subset of $X$ and the $bias$ is added. This is done throughout the input data until the output computation is complete.
0035c834 The output shapes are computed as follows. The number of channels in the output feature map is the number of kernels specified in the filter blob. The spatial height and width are computed as:
0035c8f6 $$H_{out} = (H_{in}-1)*strides[0] - 2*pads[0] + kernels[0]$$
0035c935 $$W_{out} = (W_{in}-1)*strides[1] - 2*pads[1] + kernels[1]$$
0035c973 Note on the implementation layout: conv_transpose_op_impl.h is the templated implementation of the conv_transpose_op.h file, which is why they are separate files. Also, in the implementation this operator inherits from the *ConvTransposeUnpoolOpBase* operator.
0035ca79 Github Links:
0035ca87 - https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/tree/master/caffe2/operators/conv_transpose_op.h
0035cadd - https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/tree/master/caffe2/operators/conv_transpose_op.cc
0035cb34 - https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/tree/master/caffe2/operators/conv_transpose_unpool_op_base.h

0035d9e5 Dropout
0035d9ed DropoutGrad
0035d9fb `Dropout` takes one input data tensor (`X`) and produces two tensor outputs, `Y` and
0035da50 `mask`. If the `is_test` argument is zero (default=0), the output `Y` will be the input
0035daa8 with random elements zeroed. The probability that a given element is zeroed is
0035daf7 determined by the `ratio` argument.
0035db1c If the `is_test` argument is set to non-zero, the output `Y` is exactly the same as the
0035db74 input `X`. Note that outputs are scaled by a factor of $\frac{1}{1-ratio}$ during
0035dbc6 training, so that during test time, we can simply compute an identity function. This
0035dc1b scaling is important because we want the output at test time to equal the expected value
0035dc74 at training time. Dropout has been proven to be an effective regularization technique to
0035dccd prevent overfitting during training.
0035dcf4 Github Links:

0035ee64 This op implements the exponential linear unit (ELU) activation function as described in [Fast and Accurate Deep Network Learning by Exponential Linear Units (ELUs)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.07289). The op takes an input tensor $X$ of arbitrary shape, computes the elementwise elu operation, and returns a vector $Y$ of the same shape as output. The alpha parameter may be passed as an argument, but defaults to 1. The elu operation is defined as
0035f026 $$y=f(x) =\begin{cases}\alpha(e^x-1) & x < 0 \\ x & otherwise\end{cases}$$

0036256a This op fills an output tensor with values sampled from a uniform distribution with the range determined by the desired shape of the output. 00363e26 xplat/caffe2/caffe2/operators/fully_connected_op.cc
00363e5b Same as FC, but weight matrix is supposed to be already pretransposed.
00363ea2 FCTransposed stands for calling blass with no noTrans, noTrans
00363ee3 The FC operator computes an output $(Y)$ as a linear combination of the input data blob $(X)$ with a weight blob $(W)$ and bias blob $(b)$. More formally,
00363f7f $$Y = XW^T+b$$
00363f8f Here, $X$ is a matrix of shape $(M,K)$, $W$ is a matrix of shape $(N,K)$, $b$ is a vector of length $N$, and $Y$ is a matrix of shape $(M,N)$. $N$ can be thought of as the number of nodes in the layer, $M$ is the batch size, and $K$ is the number of features in an input observation.
003640ac *NOTE: $X$ does not need to explicitly be a 2-dimensional matrix, however, if it is not it will be coerced into one. For an arbitrary $n$-dimensional tensor $X$, e.g. $[a_0, a_1, \ldots ,a_{k-1}, a_k, \ldots , a_{n-1}]$, where $a_i$ in $N$, and $k$ is the $axis$ arg provided, then $X$ will be coerced into a 2-dimensional tensor with dimensions $[a_0 * \ldots * a_{k-1}, a_k * \ldots * a_{n-1}]$. For the default case where axis=1, this means the $X$ tensor will be coerced into a 2D tensor of dimensions $[a_0, a_1 * \ldots * a_{n-1}]$, where $a_0$ is often the batch size. In this situation, we must have $a_0 = M$ and $a_1 * \ldots * a_{n-1} = K$. Lastly, even though $b$ is a vector of length $N$, it is copied and resized to shape $(M x N)$ implicitly, then added to each vector in the batch.*
003643cd Github Links:
003643db - https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/master/caffe2/operators/fully_connected_op.h
00364432 - https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/master/caffe2/operators/fully_connected_op.cc

0037316a Softmax
00373172 SoftmaxGradient
00373182 xplat/caffe2/caffe2/operators/softmax_op.cc
003731b0 Applies the Softmax function to an n-dimensional input Tensor rescaling them so
00373200 that the elements of the n-dimensional output Tensor lie in the range (0,1) and
00373250 sum to 1. The softmax operator is typically the last layer in a classifier network,
003732a4 as its output can be interpreted as confidence probabilities of an input belonging
003732f7 to each class. The input is a 2-D tensor (Tensor) of size (batch_size x
0037333f input_feature_dimensions). The output tensor has the same shape and contains the
00373390 softmax normalized values of the corresponding input. The softmax function is
003733de defined as follows:
003733f3 $$softmax(x_i) = \frac{\exp(x_i)}{\sum_{j} \exp(x_j)}$$
0037342c The input does not need to explicitly be a 2D vector; rather, it will be coerced
0037347d into one. For an arbitrary n-dimensional tensor `X` in
003734b4 $[a_0, a_1, ..., a_{k-1}, a_k, ..., a_{n-1}]$, where k is the `axis` provided,
00373503 then `X` will be coerced into a 2-dimensional tensor with dimensions
00373548 $[(a_0 * ... * a_{k-1}), (a_k * ... * a_{n-1})]$. For the default case where
00373595 `axis`=1, the `X` tensor will be coerced into a 2D tensor of dimensions
003735dd $[a_0, (a_1 * ... * a_{n-1})]$, where $a_0$ is often the batch size. In this
0037362a situation, we must have $a_0 = N$ and $a_1 * ... * a_{n-1} = D$. Each of these
00373679 dimensions must be matched correctly, or else the operator will throw errors.
003736c8 Github Links:
003736d7 - https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/master/caffe2/operators/softmax_op.h
00373726 - https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/master/caffe2/operators/softmax_op.cc

0037402e SpatialBN
00374038 xplat/caffe2/caffe2/operators/spatial_batch_norm_op.cc
00374070 Applies spatial batch normalization to the input tensor as described in the original paper, [Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training by Reducing Internal Covariate Shift](https://arxiv.org/abs/1502.03167). Be aware, this operator has two different output sets, depending on the value of *is_test*. According to the paper, the primary operation of spatial batch normalization is:
003741fc $$Y = \frac{X - \mu_x}{\sqrt{\sigma^2_{x} + \epsilon}}*\gamma + b$$
00374241 In the equation, $\mu_x$ is the *mean*, $X$ is the input data, $\sigma^2_{x}$ is the *var*, $\epsilon$ is *epsilon*, $\gamma$ is the *scale*, $b$ is the *bias*, and $Y$ is the output data. The *momentum* arg also affects this calculation in the computation of the running mean and variance. The influence of *momentum* is as follows:
00374390 $$running\_mean = running\_mean * momentum + mean * (1 - momentum)$$
003743d6 $$running\_var = running\_var * momentum + var * (1 - momentum)$$
00374419 Output when is_test = 0 (train mode): *Y, mean, var, saved_mean, saved_var*
00374466 Output when is_test = 1 (test mode): *Y*
00374490 Github Links:
0037449e - https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/master/caffe2/operators/spatial_batch_norm_op.cc
003744f9 - https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/master/caffe2/operators/spatial_batch_norm_op.h
00374555 *(type: int; default: 0)* If set to nonzero, run spatial batch normalization in test mode.
003745b0 momentum
003745b9 *(type: float; default: 0.9)* Factor used in computing the running mean and variance. e.g., running_mean = running_mean x momentum + mean x (1 - momentum)
00374654 num_batches
00374660 *(type: int; default: 1)* Specifies the number of batches to apply normalization on. Requires specifying the optional sums and sumsq inputs that provide statistics across multiple batches from which mean and variance can be determined.
0037474c The input 4-dimensional tensor of shape $NCHW$ or $NHWC$ depending on the order parameter.
003747a7 The scale as a 1-dimensional tensor of size $C$ to be applied to the output.
003747f4 The bias as a 1-dimensional tensor of size $C$ to be applied to the output.
00374840 The running mean (training) or the estimated mean (testing) as a 1-dimensional tensor of size $C$.
003748a7 The running variance (training) or the estimated variance (testing) as a 1-dimensional tensor of size $C$.
00374912 sums
00374917 *(optional)* Per-channel sums of elements to be used to determine the mean and variance for this batch.
0037497f sumsq
00374985 *(optional)* Per-channel sum of elements squared per channel to be used to determine the variance for this batch.
003749f7 The output 4-dimensional tensor of the same shape as $X$.
00374a31 The running mean after the spatial BN operator. Must be in-place with the input *mean*. Should not be used for testing.
00374aa9 The running variance after the spatial BN operator. Must be in-place with the input *var*. Should not be used for testing.
00374b24 Saved mean used during training to speed up gradient computation. Should not be used for testing.
00374b86 saved_var
00374b90 Saved variance used during training to speed up gradient computation. Should not be used for testing.

0090a2be The Conv2D operator computes a 2D convolution operation over an input blob $(X)$, with a filter blob $(filter)$ and a bias blob $(bias)$, and outputs a single output blob $(Y)$. Although there are several options for order, the convention is that the input $(X)$ is a blob of shape $(N,C_{in},H_{in},W_{in})$ and the output $(Y)$ is a blob of shape $(N,C_{out},H_{out},W_{out})$. Here, $N$ is the batch size, $C$ is the number of channels, $H$ is the spatial height, and $W$ is the spatial width. For example, if your input data was a batch of five, 100x120pixel RGB images, $X$ would have shape $(5,3,120,100)$.
0090a524 The $filter$ input blob may contain multiple filters and has shape $(M, C_{in}, K_H, K_W)$. Here, $M$ is the number of individual filters contained in the blob, $C_{in}$ is the number of channels of each filter (by convention in 2D convolution it is the same as the number of channels in the input), $K_H$ is the spatial height of the kernel, and $K_W$ is the spatial width of the kernel. The $bias$ blob is a vector of length $M$, where there is one bias for each filter in the $filter$ blob.
0090a713 Given the shape of the input blob and the filter blob, we can calculate the shape of the output blob as follows. The number of items in the batch $N$ will stay the same. The number of channels in the output will equal the number of kernels in the filter blob, so $C_{out} = M.$ With stride and pad defined below, the spatial height and width of the output ($H_{out}$ and $W_{out}$) are calculated as
0090a8a4 $$H_{out} = \left \lfloor{\frac{H_{in} - K_H + 2*pad}{stride}+1}\right \rfloor$$
0090a8f7 $$W_{out} = \left \lfloor{\frac{W_{in} - K_W + 2*pad}{stride}+1}\right \rfloor$$
0090a94a Github Links:
0090a959 - https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/master/caffe2/operators/conv_op.h
0090a9a5 - https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/master/caffe2/operators/conv_op.cc
0090a9f2 - https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/master/caffe2/operators/conv_pool_op_base.h

0090aa54 <summary> <b>Example</b> </summary>
0090aa79 **Code**
0090aa88 workspace.ResetWorkspace()
0090aaa4 op = core.CreateOperator(
0090aabe     "Conv",
0090aaca     ["X", "filter", "bias"],
0090aae7     ["Y"],
0090aaf2     kernel=5,
0090ab00     pad=1,
0090ab0b     stride=2
0090ab1b // Create X: (N,C,H,W)
0090ab32 data = np.random.randn(1,1,8,8).astype(np.float32)
0090ab65 print("Data shape: ",data.shape)
0090ab87 // Create W: (M,C,Kh,Kw)
0090aba0 filters = np.random.randn(3,1,5,5).astype(np.float32)
0090abd6 print("Filter shape: ",filters.shape)
0090abfd // Create b: M
0090ac0c bias = np.array([1.,1.,1.]).astype(np.float32)
0090ac3b print("Bias shape: ",bias.shape)
0090ac5d // Put the inputs into the workspace
0090ac82 workspace.FeedBlob("X", data)
0090aca0 workspace.FeedBlob("filter", filters)
0090acc6 workspace.FeedBlob("bias", bias)
0090ace8 // Run the operator
0090acfc workspace.RunOperatorOnce(op)
0090ad1a print("Y:\n", workspace.FetchBlob("Y"))

0090e71c consumes an input blob and applies average pooling across the the blob according
0090e76d to kernel sizes, stride sizes, pad lengths and dilation. Average pooling consists
0090e7bf of taking the average value of a subset of the input tensor according to the kernel
0090e813 size and downsampling the data into the output blob for further processing. The
0090e863 `brew` module has a wrapper for this operator for use in a `ModelHelper` object.
0090e8b5 Pooling layers reduce the spatial dimensionality of the input blob. Each of the
0090e905 output blob's dimensions will reduce according to:
0090e939 $$dim_{out}=\frac{dim_{in}-kernel+2*pad}{stride}+1$$
